definitions.gloss: time passes; time goes by; time elapses
definitions.explanation: A common expression meaning that time moves forward or a period of time has elapsed. Used to describe the passage of time in both concrete and emotional contexts.

examples.japanese: {時間|じかん}が{経|た}つのが{早|はや}い。
あれから{三年|さんねん}{時間|じかん}が{経|た}った。
examples.english: Three years have passed since then.

examples.japanese: {時間|じかん}が{経|た}つにつれて、{傷|きず}は{少|すこ}しずつ{癒|い}えていった。
examples.english: As time went by, the wound gradually healed.

notes:
One of the most frequently used time expressions in Japanese. The verb {経|た}つ ('to elapse; to pass') is specific to the passage of time and is distinct from the homophone {立|た}つ ('to stand').

USAGE:
- Often used with のが{早|はや}い to express surprise at how quickly time passes.
- The pattern {時間|じかん}が{経|た}つにつれて ('as time passes') is very common for describing gradual change.
- Can be modified with specific time periods: {一時間|いちじかん}が{経|た}つ ('one hour passes'), {長|なが}い{時間|じかん}が{経|た}つ ('a long time passes').
- In casual speech, {時間|じかん}が{経|た}つ is sometimes shortened to {時|とき}が{経|た}つ or {月日|つきひ}が{経|た}つ.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {時間|じかん}が{経|た}つのが{早|はや}い: time passes quickly
- {時間|じかん}が{経|た}つにつれて: as time goes by
- だいぶ{時間|じかん}が{経|た}った: quite some time has passed
- {時間|じかん}が{経|た}っても: even after time passes

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {月日|つきひ}が{経|た}つ: days and months pass — a more literary or reflective variant emphasizing the slow accumulation of time
- {時|とき}が{流|なが}れる: time flows — a more poetic expression
- {年月|ねんげつ}が{過|す}ぎる: years pass — emphasizes the passage of longer periods
